TokenBatch::defined¶

Back to TokenBatch API Reference

Signature¶

bool TokenBatch::defined() const noexcept

Ask Whether A Ragged Result Exists¶

defined() reports whether this handle owns a TokenBatch implementation. It is a handle-state query, not a token-count query and not a statement about the state of the nested token Note.

A default-constructed TokenBatch has no implementation and returns false. Every batch returned by a successful NLP or regex operation returns true, including a batch with zero tokens. Propagating an undefined input also returns a defined batch envelope: its tokens() Note is undefined and its canonical offsets are [0]. That representation keeps “the operation ran, but its input was absent” distinct from “no TokenBatch object was ever produced.”

The method is constant-time, performs no allocation, never inspects token bytes, and is noexcept. Use it before tokens() or offsets() when a batch may have been default constructed; those accessors reject an undefined handle. Use empty() instead when the question is whether there are any flat tokens.

Example 1: A Default Handle Is Undefined¶

const pluss::TokenBatch batch;
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << batch.defined()
          << " empty=" << batch.empty() << '\n';

Output¶

defined=false empty=true

Undefined handles are safely queryable; only payload access is invalid.

Example 2: A Populated Result Is Defined¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::note::make({"red green", "", "blue"}).nlp().tokens();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << batch.defined()
          << " empty=" << batch.empty() << '\n';

Output¶

defined=true empty=false

The empty middle source cell does not make the whole batch empty because the other cells emitted tokens.

Example 3: Defined Does Not Mean Nonempty¶

const auto batch = pluss::note::make({"", "!!!"}).nlp().tokens();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << batch.defined()
          << " empty=" << batch.empty()
          << " tokens-defined=" << batch.tokens().defined() << '\n';

Output¶

defined=true empty=true tokens-defined=true

This is a valid two-row result. Both rows are empty, represented by offsets [0, 0, 0].

Example 4: Propagated Absence Has A Defined Envelope¶

const auto batch = pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().tokens();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "batch-defined=" << batch.defined()
          << " tokens-defined=" << batch.tokens().defined()
          << " empty=" << batch.empty() << '\n';

Output¶

batch-defined=true tokens-defined=false empty=true

Check the nested tokens().defined() when absence must remain distinguishable from a present input that simply emitted no tokens.

See Also¶

  • empty: test whether the flat token payload has zero elements.

  • tokens: access the flattened payload after checking state.

  • offsets: recover each source cell’s token range.
